topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic contains the lecturer's opening remarks, course overview, and learning objectives for the lecture on the causes of cancer.

topics.label: The Nature of Cancer and the Balance Between Intrinsic and Environmental Causes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the biological basis of cancer development and explore the relative contributions of intrinsic cellular processes, genetics, and environmental exposures to overall cancer risk.

topics.label: Pathogens and Infectious Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens drive carcinogenesis, detailing the collaborative role of Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical, Dietary, and Radiation Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which chemical carcinogens and radiation interact with cellular metabolism to induce DNA damage and mutational changes.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concept of tumor promotion, demonstrating how non-mutagenic stimuli and chronic inflammation facilitate the outgrowth of primed cells.

topics.label: Host Developmental Timing and Summary of Carcinogenic Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue developmental stage and host timing dictate susceptibility to carcinogens, concluding with a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect and prove the carcinogenicity of environmental agents.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks, the challenges of determining carcinogenic potency, and the daily balance of risk versus benefit.
